rules.rationale: Small heterocycles maximize polar surface area per atom, the dominant hydration driver.
Large halogenated solutes have low polar surface area and poor water packing.
Aromatic surfaces hydrate poorly, so aromaticity should lower hydration affinity.
Ring-free acyclic scaffolds pack well in water, raising hydration affinity.

skills.hypothesis: Counter-hypothesis: hydration affinity tracks polar surface area, not size. Fails if the source smiles_length effect (+6.89/-6.61/-11.46) carries across.

rules.rationale: Hydrogen-bond donors (heteroatoms) donate water hydrogen bonds, raising hydration affinity.
Halogen substitution weakens hydrogen bonding, reducing hydration affinity.
Aromatic surfaces hydrate poorly, so aromaticity should lower hydration affinity.
Ring-rich molecules pack poorly in water, lowering hydration affinity; source ring_bin transferred strongly (w=0.76).

skills.hypothesis: Transfers ESOL hydrogen-bonding effects: heteroatom-rich, halogen-poor, aromatic-poor, ring-poor candidates score highest. Fails if hydration affinity tracks polar surface area rather than hydrogen bonding.

lesson: Across four development seeds, the polar-surface-area counter-hypothesis skill dropped sharply from generation 0 (mean AUC 81.17) to generation 1 (mean AUC 61.21), while the size-and-heteroatom transfer skill held steady (mean AUC 69.37 to 67.86). This suggests the polar-surface-area mechanism was too fragile to carry across, so the safer transfer is hydrogen bonding.
revision_summary: Retained the polar-surface-area counter-hypothesis skill unchanged as v3, since its core mechanism remains the strongest mechanistic prior. Replaced the deployed size-transfer skill with a hydrogen-bonding transfer that keeps the heteroatom bonus and ring penalty but drops the uncertain smiles_length term, so the deployed skill now transfers hydrogen bonding rather than size.
